description: Mine gliders, blinkers, and collision motifs from small CA rules, then reinterpret them as portable witness fragments: worldlines become repeated copy interfaces and collisions become candidate certificate births. This yields a reusable gadget library before full witness assembly.
mathematical_formalization: For a rule F let M(F) be the set of periodic localized spacetime motifs modulo translation and phase. A decoder D maps m\in M(F) to partial witness deltas (\Delta f,\Delta R,\Delta T). Search motif multisets maximizing \Delta(n-t)/(\Delta m+\Delta r) subject to compatibility and constructibility constraints.
analogical_connections: Motif libraries as arithmetic gadget catalogs.
implementation_hypothesis: Use Wuensche-style exhaustive motif search or SAT-enumerated short orbits to populate a motif database, cluster motifs by decoded effect, and compose only the highest-yield motifs into larger recursive scaffolds.
experiment_seed: Enumerate motifs up to bounding box 6x6x8 for a small reversible or conservative rule family and compare motif-composed witnesses against direct random full-witness search.

closest_prior_art.title: Pattern Problems related to the Arithmetic Kakeya Conjecture

novelty_claim: The new step is decoding dynamical motifs into arithmetic proof fragments instead of treating them as purely dynamical curiosities.
differentiation: Motif discovery is only accepted when the motifs integrate into exact constructible graphs and forcing pairs with measurable score.
